articles.title: Orchid Shift Pearl
articles.summary: Loud candy flip: magenta and teal patches shift across the panel in a chaotic mottled mosaic, very sparkly. Reads as a loud magenta and blue confetti, like purple that is trying to be two colours at once; the mix averages to a vivid violet-blue with warm pink flares.
articles.what: Candy-pearl that shifts candy magenta to candy teal across the surface — fine mica platelets carry the two-tone flip. Up close: Patchwork of irregular polygon platelets 20-60px in two families: hot magenta-orchid with pink veins and electric blue-cyan with lime-teal mottling, with tiny pale dots like pearl beads dotted over. Edges are sharp and slightly dark; each patch has soft internal cloudiness. From a distance: Reads as a loud magenta and blue confetti, like purple that is trying to be two colours at once; the mix averages to a vivid violet-blue with warm pink flares. Measured spec (average): metal 145, roughness 56, coat 16. Shine: high gloss. Metal: medium. It brings its own colours.
when: Best on: body, hero panel, hood.
Fits: show car, gt / sports car, open wheel.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Orchid Shift Pearl" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Leave BASE COLOR on Use finish's own color to keep its colours.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: colour shift is strongest on big curved panels
Hood, roof and fenders show the two-tone best
Numbers need a solid white or black block with a thick outline; the high-contrast patchwork cuts through thin digits.
None or one big soft fade: the platelet mosaic is already loud
Pairs well with: black, chrome, white, silver.
pitfalls: Not a smooth colour-shift paint: it shows distinct patches in two colours, not a gradient
Not holographic rainbow: the palette is magenta and blue-cyan
Avoid: numbers and small text over the busy pattern, other loud flip finishes nearby.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 145 (strong pearl or anodized metal), roughness 56 (high gloss), clearcoat 16 (maximum clearcoat). The spec is textured, not flat: metal vary by 20 or more across the surface.
articles.intent_note: Spec-driven shelf: the shine does all the visual work and your own paint colour stays as it is.
articles.paint_advice: It brings its own colours, so leave BASE COLOR on the finish's own colour. Put it next to a plain zone of the opposite sheen (matte beside gloss, warm beside cool) so the colours have a calm neighbour. Avoid: numbers and small text over the busy pattern, other loud flip finishes nearby.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: none or one big soft fade: the platelet mosaic is already loud; large plain stripes in black or white: calm area to read
Patterns to avoid: flake, mosaic or voronoi patterns: double the patchwork; fine line patterns: moire with the platelets
Spec overlays that work: gloss clear boost: already near max; fine sparkle spec: adds pearl glints
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

Any bold graphic, stripe or number: crisp edges on smooth pearl
Pairs well with: chrome trim, dark base, gold accents, white.
pitfalls: Not mirror chrome or full metallic: only half metal
Not satin or matte: it is high gloss
Avoid: heavy flake textures, matte overlays.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 100 (pearl-level metal), roughness 40 (high gloss), clearcoat 16 (maximum clearcoat). The spec is almost perfectly flat, one smooth material.
articles.intent_note: Spec-driven shelf: the shine does all the visual work and your own paint colour stays as it is.
articles.paint_advice: Pearl depth shows best on a clear mid-tone or deep saturated colour; a dull grey paint hides the shift. Avoid: heavy flake textures, matte overlays.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: any bold graphic, stripe or number: crisp edges on smooth pearl; gloss-contrast stripes in matte: classic pearl and matte contrast
Patterns to avoid: flake or glitter patterns: fight the clean pearl; mirror chrome overlays: lose the half-metal subtlety
Spec overlays that work: pearl flake or shimmer sweeps: add actual pearl shift on top; fine micro grain: subtle tooth
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.

articles.title: Powder Coat
articles.summary: Smooth semi-matte film with a subdued diffuse sheen and no sparkle; low-glare surface that keeps your colour flat and even. Reads as plain painted metal with a low, even, slightly dull sheen, like industrial powder coating; no sparkle, no shimmer, no reflections you could point at.
articles.what: Thick powder coating (10/120/145) — eggshell sheen with the clearcoat suppressed. Industrial and tactical builds. Up close: Nothing to see up close: a perfectly even, texture-free surface with no grain, flake or pattern. Spec is uniform (metal about 10, roughness about 120, clearcoat about 143 with zero variation), so it is only a flat eggshell sheen on your own paint. From a distance: Reads as plain painted metal with a low, even, slightly dull sheen, like industrial powder coating; no sparkle, no shimmer, no reflections you could point at. Measured spec (average): metal 10, roughness 120, coat 143. Shine: semi-matte. Metal: none. It takes the colour you give the zone.
when: Fits: truck / off-road, dirt late model, stock car.
how: Click the zone you want to change.
Click the BASE MATERIAL box (it says "Click to choose a base") and type "Powder Coat" in the SEARCH FINISHES box.
Click it to open the big preview, then click Apply.
Pick your colour with BASE COLOR.
Render and judge it on the car, not on the swatch.
tips: Whole body: a uniform sheen looks best across all panels
Wheels or trim for a tool-grade look
Numbers read cleanly in any colour; the dull even surface gives no glare or texture to fight them.
Any pattern or graphics: a pure spec base never competes with them
Pairs well with: black, olive, grey, restrained chrome.
pitfalls: Not matte flat black or a soft matte: sheen is a touch higher, eggshell
Not satin pearl or metallic: metal is near zero, no sparkle
Avoid: high-gloss clearcoats, overpowering reflective trim.
articles.spec_character: Average spec: metal 10 (non-metal paint), roughness 120 (satin or eggshell), clearcoat 143 (dull or trace clearcoat).
articles.intent_note: Spec-driven shelf: the shine does all the visual work and your own paint colour stays as it is.
articles.paint_advice: Gloss shows the paint colour as it is, so any colour works; pick the colour for contrast with the neighbouring zones, not for the finish. Avoid: high-gloss clearcoats, overpowering reflective trim.

combos.why: Patterns that suit it: any pattern or graphics: a pure spec base never competes with them; fine grain or stipple pattern: faking textured industrial coat
Patterns to avoid: chrome-style or mirror patterns: dull base kills their point
Spec overlays that work: fine micro-texture or orange-peel spec: gives the powder-coat bumpiness this base lacks; gloss/matte stripe spec: sheen contrast without colour change
Judge the paint and the shine together: the same spec looks different under different colours.
